title: Questions and Answers
subtitle: The most common questions about me.

questions.a: wakku is the name of Walker's musical project. Behind the character is Alan, someone passionate about music. Through wakku, Alan creates original content and music, exploring different sounds and styles.

The name 'wakku' emerged spontaneously one day when I was looking for a name for my musical project. I asked some friends for ideas, and one of them said 'What about waku waku?' I liked the sound and the resemblance to 'Walker', so I adopted it. Over time, it evolved into 'wakku'. It doesn't have a specific meaning, but I like to relate it to the Japanese word 'waku' which means 'to sprout' or 'to flow'. Or also to the expression 'waku waku' which is used to describe the emotion or anticipation of something fun or exciting.

questions.q: How do you prefer to be called?
questions.a: Walker or wakku is fine. In general, I don't have a strict preference, so you can use whichever feels most comfortable to you.

questions.q: Since when have you been making music?
questions.a: I started around 2021 experimenting and exploring different styles and sounds, but it was at the end of 2022 when I began to take music more seriously and consistently. Since then, I have been creating, improving, and regularly publishing music.

questions.q: Do you have any formal musical training?
questions.a: I don't have formal musical training, but I have learned a lot through practice, some online tutorials, experimentation, and interaction with other musicians. If you ask me if I know how to read sheet music, the answer is no, but that hasn't stopped me from creating music I like and others enjoy.

questions.q: What inspires you to make music?
questions.a: I am inspired by many things, from my own emotions and experiences to the music of other artists I admire. I also like to experiment with sounds and see what I can create from them. The idea of sharing something I have created with others is also a great motivation for me.

I am inspired by many artists. Some of my favorite artists include Virtual Riot, Eliminate, Skrillex, Teminite and Knock2. I am also inspired by friends like alwk, thwl, Demonstep, Maiandraw, Diaman, among others.

questions.q: Do you do everything by yourself?
questions.a: When it comes to composition, mixing and mastering, yes, I do everything by myself when it's not about collaborations. When it comes to visualizers or illustrations, I often collaborate with other artists in order to speed up the process and achieve better results. For example, my logo was designed by CoraBitz, and some illustrations for visualizers have been made by friends like Ratypea250 or artists from the projects I collaborate on.

questions.q: What is your long-term goal with wakku?
questions.a: My long-term goal with wakku is to continue creating music and content that I am passionate about, and eventually move on from the Friday Night Funkin' community. I would like to build a community of fans and collaborators who enjoy what I do and feel inspired to create their own things. In the future, I would like to explore different forms of art and creative expression, and see how far I can take this project.

questions.q: Who is the anime girl that appears in your profiles?
questions.a: She is Lia, an original character created by me, representing the visual identity of wakku. She has become an important symbol for the project. She appears in profiles and other graphic materials related to wakku.

She does, but it's something I want to keep secret for now. What I can say is that she is an android with a human soul and mind made by a secret organization that was seeking immortality. Eventually, I will be adding a section dedicated to my characters where I will reveal more information about her and other characters in my universe.

No, Lia is not my sona. She is a character that represents the visual identity of wakku, but she is not a direct representation of myself. My sona is Walker, he is the closest representation of Alan both inside and outside the universe of wakku.
